inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped duplicate check filters groups with HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT group_id) greater than one.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as a team membership report. A LEFT JOIN retains teams with no assignments before HAVING filters to teams with at least two distinct active members; duplicate assignment rows and NULL member IDs exercise COUNT(DISTINCT) semantics. The fixture schema, rows, and output purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Team 10 has two distinct active members plus a duplicate assignment and an inactive assignment; team 20 has one active member plus a NULL member ID; team 30 has no assignments; team 40 has exactly two distinct active members. HAVING must retain only teams 10 and 40.
determinism_notes: The report is ordered by the unique team ID and uses no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE teams (team_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE team_members (assignment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_id INT NOT NULL, member_id INT, active TINYINT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT t.team_id, t.team_name, COUNT(DISTINCT tm.member_id) AS active_member_count FROM teams t LEFT JOIN team_members tm ON tm.team_id = t.team_id AND tm.active = 1 GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT tm.member_id) >= 2 ORDER BY t.team_id
